newsitem.title: USA: PP&L seeks end of separate energy charge.
newsitem.headline: PP&L seeks end of separate energy charge.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co said Friday it asked the state Public Utility Commission to approve rate structure changes that would eliminate a fluctuating energy charge on customer bills.

The requested changes will result in no change in the total charges to customers, the PP&L Resources Inc subsidiary said, explaining it is requesting the commission permit it to roll the current energy cost rate, a separate component of customer bills, into the base rates.
"The energy cost rate has been in place to allow utilities to adjust customer bills annually to reflect the changes in the cost of fuel needed to produce electricity," the utility explained.

"The customer choice legislation signed by Gov. Ridge earlier this month places a cap on rates beginning next month. That cap means that it is no longer appropriate to have this separate fluctuating charge on customer bills."
The company said it also is requesting approval to roll all state tax charges into base rates. Today, some state taxes are shown on customer bills as a separate charge.
Spokesman Dan McCarthy said the company is moving to end regulatory limits on its accounting.

With these changes, he explained, taxes may be shown on bills when they are unbundled at some future time, but a rate case before the commission will not be needed for changes in amounts collected for taxes.
